packageRules.description: Supply-chain inputs (actions, container images) are always human-reviewed; label them for triage.
Org practice: automerge patch-level Go module updates once every check passes. platformAutomerge=false makes Renovate itself wait for all checks, independent of repo auto-merge settings.
Let new module and action releases age before proposing them, so a compromised or yanked release is usually caught upstream first. Docker registries without timestamps are excluded.
Actions are pinned to full-semver tags, so a digest-only change means the tag was moved (the tj-actions pattern). Never a routine PR: require explicit approval on the dependency dashboard.

go.mod's go directive is capped by golangci-lint, not by what Go has released: the linter refuses to load a module targeting a newer Go than the linter was itself built with. Raising it is a deliberate change made together with the lint job's go-version and a linter that supports it, so keep it off Renovate's routine queue. See the comment on go-version in .github/workflows/lint.yml.

The builder image may run ahead of the go directive (builder >= directive is the invariant), but a major or minor bump still has to clear the same linter constraint, so it is reviewed rather than automerged.
golangci-lint sets the ceiling on the Go version this repository can use, in the Makefile and the lint workflow together. Group them so the two pins never drift apart.
Runtime base image: digest-pinned, and a digest-only refresh is the normal way it moves.

customManagers.description: golangci-lint version mirrored in the Makefile and the lint workflow; both must move together.
